tests.scope: Tiny temporary archive/prune fixtures; all service/mount queries mocked.

checks: Fixed SHA-bound inventory and closure evidence admit only card0/card3 restore20..28 torch_compile_cache files; logs/state/overlays/modelinfos/model/research results and restore29 excluded.
Copy and prune have separate exclusive attempt receipts; neither retries or overwrites previous operation artifacts.
Actual operations must compare all three current active/running service argv and working directories against pinned restore29 configuration, with bounded read-only systemctl queries.
Exact external mount UUID/source/fstype/parent inode and 50GiB reserve, plus source+32MiB archive allowance before copy, are required.
Every tar member extent and SHA, complete member set and whole archive hash are verified; originals are rehashed after copy and independently before pruning.
Recovery archive descriptor remains open, with inode/path/stamp rechecks before each unlink.
All eighteen sibling incomplete-cache markers and full restore map are file- and directory-fsynced before any deletion; permission refusal precedes markers.
Per-file SHA/stamp plus no-follow held parent FD and final relative inode check precede each unlink; parent directory fsynced after unlink.
Symlinks, hardlinks, unexpected files/directories and observed identity drift are refused. No directory deletion or service mutation is implemented.
Documentation retains exact 4.26MB original inventory permanently and describes separate-directory reconstruction and prohibition on silently rebuilding pins after partial pruning.
limits: Historical restore20..22 stop/inactive logs are weaker than complete privileged owner inventories; later complete drains corroborate closure.
Current service configuration is checked only by the future root-run operation. This review performed no real service/mount queries, archive copy, cache hashing or pruning.
Trusted coordinator must avoid concurrent reuse/reconfiguration; metadata/FD checks are not an atomic filesystem transaction or a proof against hostile same-user races.
A crash after unlink can precede final per-file accounting; durable complete restore maps and archive preserve recovery.

If writing the failure receipt itself fails, that secondary exception can supersede the original operation exception, matching pinned parent behavior. The durable start receipt/markers remain and no successful result is returned.
